name: Cinnamon-Buff
lede: Cinnamon-Buff is a warm, moderate orange yellow named for the spice, recorded in Robert Ridgway's 1912 color standard and carried into the ISCC-NBS system of 1955.

sections.title: A Ridgway cinnamon
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* lists Cinnamon-Buff on plate XXIX, hue 17′′, tone b [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 places the same swatch in block 71, the category it calls moderate orange yellow, 5.0 units from that block's centroid [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[yellowish-camel]], [[peachbeige]], [[sand-yellow]] and [[saratoga]], at 2.8, 3.8, 8, 3.8, 4.1 and 4.4 ΔE [2]. All three borrow the word from [[cinnamon]], the spice [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Cinnamon-Buff covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 1,240 of them, about 5.2 per cent, as photographed [3]. It plays a highlight far more often than a shadow, in 91 per cent of its appearances [3]. It is especially common in Mughal painting, 69 of 168 works, 7.9 times the archive rate, and more broadly across Indian painting, 137 of 721 works [3]. These are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen color, not a pigment identification [3].
